sections.h2: Where to take a Venango County deed
sections.html:
Deeds go through the Register and Recorder office in the county courthouse, 1168 Liberty Street, Franklin, PA 16323. The mailing address is P.O. Box 831. The office opens on weekdays at 8:30 in the morning, closes at 4:30 in the afternoon and shuts for legal holidays.

The same elected office is also Register of Wills and Clerk of Orphans' Court, so probate filings, marriage licenses and real estate recordings all run through one courthouse counter. A seller dealing with an inherited house will often visit for both reasons.

Yes, Venango County deeds can be recorded electronically. Electronic filing of real estate documents is handled by CSC eRecording Solutions, reachable at 866-652-0111. Title companies and attorneys commonly use it because it skips the courthouse trip and the mail time, and it works well when buyer and seller sign in different places.

Fees depend on the document, so contact the office for the fee or for a fee schedule. The county also posts a Recorder of Deeds fee schedule in its document library. Call the office for the exact total on your deed before you send payment.

sections.h2: Transfer tax in a Venango County sale
sections.html:
The recorder collects it when the deed is filed. The state's share is 1 percent of the value, and the person conveying and the person receiving the property both answer for it. Local governments can add a tax of their own and split it between school districts and municipalities.

  • Exempt transfers include some family gifts, transfers to government bodies and property passed by will or intestacy.
  • The sales contract sets who pays in practice, so read that clause before you sign.

The county has two cities, Franklin and Oil City, plus boroughs and townships, and the local share depends on where the parcel sits. Ask the recorder which municipality and school district your parcel falls in before you work out your net proceeds.

Venango County has been losing residents for decades. Its population peaked at 65,328 in 1950 and stood at 50,454 in 2020. The mid-2025 estimate is 49,346, down 2.2 percent from the 2020 base. The county counts 26,293 housing units serving 21,397 households, and owners live in 75.3 percent of homes.

The typical owned home is worth $119,800, rent at the midpoint is $795 a month, and household income at the midpoint is $61,522. About 27.2 percent of residents are 65 or older. With values near $119,800, a house that needs work faces a modest price ceiling, and repair costs can eat most of the gain. Few new homes are built in the county, so most buyers choose among existing houses.

sections.h2: Old deeds, easements and oil history
sections.html:
The county is tied to the start of the oil industry, and its older parcels often carry old deeds, old easements and mineral questions. A title search matters on a long-held parcel. Ask your title company to look for recorded easements, rights of way and releases ahead of closing.

A seller with an older house in Franklin or Oil City should also expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at the foundation, wiring and plumbing.

The county has two cities, Franklin, which is the seat, and Oil City, the largest place. Boroughs include Sugar Creek, Pleasantville, Polk, Emlenton, Rouseville, Clintonville, Cooperstown, Barkeyville and Utica. Cranberry and Cornplanter are the two most populous townships.

Each has its own government, so zoning, permit rules and local tax shares depend on the address. Before listing, call the borough, city or township office that covers your house and ask what an inspector or buyer is likely to raise. The recorder's staff can tell you which municipality and school district a parcel belongs to when the deed is filed.

The county publishes a Real Estate Tax Millages page with a PDF for every year from 2005 through 2026. Check the latest sheet for your municipality and school district, since the millage that applies to a house depends on where it sits. Ask the county's Tax Assessment Office, also in the courthouse complex, about the assessed value behind that bill.

Buyers will ask for the figures, so keep your last tax bill handy when you talk to a title company. A seller who would rather skip repairs can consider a direct as-is cash purchase, since fixing an older home can cost more than the market returns.

When a house comes through an estate, the Register of Wills handles probate and collects inheritance tax for the Commonwealth, and in this county that is the same office that records the deed. Confirm who has authority to sign before anyone schedules a closing. A transfer by will or intestacy can be exempt from transfer tax, so ask the recorder which paperwork applies.

Because one counter covers both tasks, an executor can often start the probate filing and ask recording questions in the same visit.

After you accept an offer, the title company or attorney orders payoff figures, searches title for easements and releases, and prepares the deed. At closing you sign before a notary. The deed is then sent for recording, electronically through CSC eRecording Solutions or in person at the Liberty Street office. The transfer tax is collected when the deed is filed, and the Recorder indexes it so the new owner's name appears in the county records.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, which shortens the timeline, but title work and recording still apply. Keep your tax bill, payoff letter and a copy of the recorded deed in one folder.

faqs.q: When is the Venango County recorder open?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., closed on legal holidays, in the courthouse at 1168 Liberty Street in Franklin.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available in Venango County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county names CSC eRecording Solutions as the processor of electronic real estate filings, at 866-652-0111. Your title company or attorney can usually set this up.

faqs.q: Where are the Venango County recording fees listed?
faqs.a: The county posts a Recorder of Deeds fee schedule in its document library. You can also contact the Register and Recorder's office for fees, and it is wise to call before you send a check.

faqs.q: Who handles probate for a Venango County house?
faqs.a: The Register of Wills handles probate and collects inheritance tax for the Commonwealth. In Venango County that office is combined with the Recorder and the Clerk of Orphans' Court.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rate applies in Venango County?
faqs.a: The state's piece is 1 percent of the value. A municipality and school district may add shares, so ask the recorder for the combined rate on your parcel.
